title: The Voice Memo I Recorded After the Layoffs
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] It's eleven at night, and I just found out my entire department was eliminated this morning, so I'm recording this instead of texting anyone, because I don't trust my own words right now.
Narrator: If you had asked me last week whether my job was secure, I would have said absolutely, without hesitation, which shows how little we actually control.
Narrator: [gently] What strikes me most isn't the shock itself, but how quickly my mind jumped to blame, as though someone must be at fault for something only Allah ultimately decreed.
Narrator: I kept thinking, if I had switched teams last year like a colleague suggested, none of this would have happened to me specifically.
Narrator: [reflective] However, that thinking leads nowhere useful, because it assumes I could have outrun a decision that was already written for me.
Narrator: So instead, I'm trying to hold two things at once tonight, genuine grief over the loss, and genuine trust that this loss has a purpose I simply cannot see yet.
Narrator: [honestly] My father once told me that qadar isn't an excuse to stop trying, it's a reason to stop drowning when trying doesn't work out the way we planned.
Narrator: Despite understanding that intellectually, I still feel afraid about rent, about explaining this to my parents, about starting over at thirty-four.

Narrator: [calmly] Even though the fear is real, I noticed something else sitting underneath it, a strange, quiet confidence that I have survived uncertain seasons before and found my footing eventually.
Narrator: As a result, tomorrow I'll update my resume, apply to three companies, and pray fajr with real attention instead of rushing through it like I usually do.
Narrator: [encouraging] In spite of everything that happened today, I refuse to let this become proof that I was abandoned, because losing a job is not the same as losing Allah's care.
Narrator: If tomorrow brings another rejection, then I'll record another memo like this one, and I'll keep reminding myself of the same simple truth until I actually believe it fully.

quiz.question: Why is the narrator recording a voice memo instead of texting anyone?
options: He wants to practice public speaking
He doesn't trust his own words right now
quiz.explanation: He says he doesn't trust his own words right now, so he records a memo instead of texting.

quiz.question: What thought does the narrator notice himself having, and then reject?
options: That switching teams last year would have prevented this happening to him
That his boss was always fair
That he never liked the job anyway
quiz.explanation: He catches himself thinking that switching teams last year would have prevented this, then recognizes that thinking leads nowhere useful.

quiz.question: What did the narrator's father tell him about qadar?
options: It isn't an excuse to stop trying, it's a reason to stop drowning when trying fails
It means you should never try
It only applies to wealthy people
It has nothing to do with daily struggles
quiz.explanation: His father told him qadar isn't an excuse to stop trying, it's a reason to stop drowning when trying doesn't work out.

quiz.question: What does the narrator plan to do tomorrow?
options: Update his resume, apply to companies, and pray fajr with real attention
quiz.explanation: He plans to update his resume, apply to three companies, and pray fajr with real attention.

quiz.question: What does the narrator refuse to believe about losing his job?
options: That it was his fault entirely
That it means he was abandoned by Allah
That he will ever find another job
quiz.explanation: He refuses to let the job loss become proof he was abandoned, insisting it is not the same as losing Allah's care.

quiz.question: What event caused the narrator’s shock?
quiz.explanation: The job loss begins the reflection.

quiz.question: Why does the narrator question blaming?
options: It cannot undo the event or provide a useful response
quiz.explanation: The script redirects blame toward action.

quiz.question: Which response is presented as responsible?
options: Updating plans and seeking lawful next steps
quiz.explanation: Faith is paired with practical action.

quiz.question: What does qadar not remove?
options: The duty to make thoughtful choices

quiz.question: What is rejected at the end?
options: That job loss proves Allah has abandoned someone
quiz.explanation: Hardship is not a verdict on a person.
